r.경제 체제: Market economy · platinum, gold and coal mining, finance, high unemployment

r.정치 구도: Voters choose parties, and the resulting parliament elects the president. After apartheid, the system of racial segregation, ended in 1994, the African National Congress (ANC) held a majority throughout, but in the 2024 election it lost its majority for the first time and formed a coalition government with the Democratic Alliance and other parties. Corruption, power shortages and high unemployment have fed discontent with the government. Many local councils also have no majority party.

t.why: One of Africa's most industrialized countries and the only African member of the G20 as a country. As a BRICS member it speaks for emerging economies with China, Russia, India and Brazil, and in 2023 it took Israel to the International Court of Justice for violating the Genocide Convention in the Gaza war. It sits on the Cape of Good Hope route linking the Atlantic and Indian oceans, the detour ships take when the Red Sea is blocked. It is rich in minerals needed for the car and hydrogen industries, such as platinum, manganese and chrome.
t.rel: The center of the southern African economy and a BRICS member. In 2023 it took Israel to the International Court of Justice on genocide charges, and in 2025 it went through a diplomatic clash with the United States.
t.korea: The two established relations in 1992. South Africa sent an air force squadron to fight in the Korean War. Korea sells it cars and machinery and buys coal and minerals. Koreans also know it as host of the 2010 World Cup.
t.know: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria for the executive, Cape Town for the legislature and Bloemfontein for the judiciary.
etext: Its output of platinum, manganese and chrome is among the largest in the world, and it mines a lot of gold, coal and iron ore. It has the know-how to run very deep mines.
It has Africa's largest stock market, banks and insurers, serving as the gateway for investment on the continent. It also has many car assembly plants.
Problems at the state power company caused years of rolling blackouts, and railways and ports are old. Unemployment is among the highest in the world, and income inequality is wide.
